newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Li thanks African nations, plans visit.
newsitem.headline: China's Li thanks African nations, plans visit.

text.p: Chinese Premier Li Peng on Monday thanked African nations for helping to block a U.N. motion critical of Beijing's human rights record, saying he would tour six countries on the continent next month.
Li would visit Zambia, Mozambique, Gabon, Cameroon, Nigeria and Tanzania between May 5 and May 14, state radio said.

It quoted Li as thanking ambassadors of the six nations for their support in sinking a resolution brought by the United States and Western allies at the United Nations last week that aimed to censure China for widespread human rights abuses.

Beijing rallied strong support from Third World countries at the U.N. Human Rights Commission in Geneva to block the motion and has since exacted retribution on smaller European nations that backed the resolution by cancelling diplomatic exchanges.

China was a reliable friend of African nations and was willing to expand cooperation, state radio quoted Li as telling the six ambassadors during a meeting at the Zhongnanhai leaders' compound in Beijing.
The ambassadors had congratulated Li on what they called China's successful defence of its sovereignty at the Geneva commission, it said.
China dismisses all public criticism of its human rights record as interference in its internal affairs.
Beijing has close relations with many African nations, which have long benefited from Chinese development aid and have proved important diplomatic allies in international organisations.
Li would make a working visit to the Seychelles from May 3-4, state radio said but gave no details.
